question: Will the winner of the 2026 American League MVP Award be a unanimous selection?

calls.reasoning: Base rate: ~4/12 AL MVPs unanimous 2014-2025; ~4/6 when the winner was an overwhelming favorite. But MLB.com's final staff poll (Sept 22) gave Alvarez only 29/38 first-place votes (Caminero 7, Witt 1, Schlittler 1), unlike the near-unanimous polls before the Ohtani/Judge sweeps. Alvarez is a pure DH who slumped late (.264/.840 OPS over 41 games); Caminero (3B, 42 HR, ~5.7 bWAR, strong Rays team) and Witt (AL WAR leader) are credible picks for dissenting first-place votes. Win markets (~96% Polymarket/Kalshi) don't price unanimity; no unanimity market found. Even a modest per-voter defection rate across 30 ballots makes a sweep unlikely; slight allowance for voters consolidating after his strong final line (.316/42 HR, MLB-leading OPS).
calls.dossier:
- MLB.com final 2026 MVP staff poll (Sept 22, 2026), 38 voters: Alvarez 29 first-place votes/181 pts; Caminero 7/149; Witt 1/62; Schlittler 1/60; Rice 0/40. It noted that over his last 41 games (as of Sept 22) Alvarez hit .264 with an .840 OPS.
- Alvarez final 2026 line (per question background / Yahoo, Oct 28, 2026): .316/.432/.601, 42 HR, 106 RBI, 109 BB (33 IBB); AL batting title; led MLB in OBP, SLG and OPS. Primary DH.
- Caminero (Rays 3B): 42 HR, 101 RBI, .276, ~5.7 bWAR (search summary); Rays were MLB's best team in August (CBS).
- Witt Jr.: AL WAR leader among position players (6.6 per MLB.com in Sept), elite defense and baserunning.
- CBS Sports (Aug 2026, Matt Snyder): the race may not be the blowout the odds suggest; Alvarez's fWAR lead was tiny and he trailed in bWAR at the time; DH-only profile is his vulnerability.
- Players Choice (Oct 28, 2026): Alvarez won AL Outstanding Player over Caminero and Witt, plus AL Comeback Player.
- BBWAA finalists announced Nov 2, 2026; winner announced Nov 12. Ballots were cast before the postseason.
- Win markets (Polymarket, Kalshi) price only whether Alvarez wins, not unanimity; no unanimity market found.
- Base rates over AL MVP 2014-2025 (all winners): unanimous 4/12 (Trout 2014, Ohtani 2021, Ohtani 2023, Judge 2024). Over heavy-favorite winners only: roughly 4/6 (non-unanimous examples: Judge 2022 28/30, Betts 2018 28/30). Over 2015-2020 winners: 0/6 unanimous.
- Status quo: the winner gets at least one non-first-place vote unless voters consolidate fully.
- Resolves off the BBWAA official ballot breakdown (bbwaa.com/awards) or MLB.com totals; requires all ballots counted to list the winner first.
- Event window: the Nov 12, 2026 announcement; ballots already cast, outcome fixed but unknown.
- Searched but not found: any leaked BBWAA ballots, voter commentary on unanimity, or a market specifically on unanimity; the ESPN article on Alvarez did not load.

calls.reasoning: Alvarez is a ~96-99% favorite to win, but unanimity requires all 30 BBWAA writers to rank him first. Base rate of AL MVP unanimity 2000-2025 is ~15% overall, higher (~40-50%) for heavy favorites, but even heavy favorites (Judge 2022, 28/30) drop votes. The key signal: MLB.com's final 38-expert poll had 9 non-Alvarez first-place votes (7 Caminero, 1 Witt, 1 Schlittler), far from the near-unanimous polls preceding past unanimous winners. Witt essentially ties him in WAR (bWAR 6.7 vs 6.8; fWAR tied 6.8), Alvarez is a primary DH and slumped late (.840 OPS last 41 games), and Caminero hit 42 HR at 3B, so a few dissenting first-place votes look likely. Polymarket only prices winning (0.96); no market on unanimity was found.

calls.reasoning: Alvarez is a near-lock to win (Polymarket ~96%), but unanimity requires all 30 BBWAA first-place votes. The final MLB.com expert poll (Sept 22) gave him only 29/38 first-place votes (~24% elsewhere), down from 34/37 in late Aug, after a weaker September. Witt Jr. led AL position players in WAR (~6.2-6.4 vs Alvarez ~5.7-5.8 bWAR/fWAR), Caminero hit 42 HR at 3B, and Alvarez is a primary DH who did not lead in HR. Historically AL unanimity (3 of 2021-25) occurred when no rival had a WAR-based case; 2022 Judge lost 2 to Ohtani. BBWAA is often more consolidated than media polls, which keeps this above ~5%.

calls.reasoning: Alvarez is a ~96% favorite to win, but unanimity needs all 30 BBWAA first-place votes. Base rate for heavy-favorite AL MVPs being unanimous is ~4/6, but those cases had near-unanimous media polls; MLB.com's final 38-expert poll gave Alvarez only 29/38 firsts (7 Caminero, 1 Witt, 1 Schlittler), down from 34/37 in August after a late slump. Primary-DH profile, Witt's comparable WAR and Caminero's 42 HR at 3B make at least one dissenting BBWAA first-place vote likely. BBWAA consolidation and Alvarez's strong final line keep this from going lower; a small chance he doesn't win at all also drags it down.
calls.reconciliation: All runs agree on the core facts: ballots were cast before the postseason, there is no unanimity market, and the Sept 22 MLB.com poll had 29/38 first-place votes for Alvarez. The only factual conflict is WAR (Run 3: Witt ahead ~6.2-6.4 vs ~5.7-5.8 in September; Run 2: final bWAR Alvarez 6.8 vs Witt 6.7, fWAR tied). These likely reflect different dates; I couldn't settle it without web access, but either way Witt has a close WAR-based case, which supports dissenting votes. The rest is judgment: how much BBWAA voting consolidates compared with media polls. A ~24% non-Alvarez share in the expert poll implies that even a several-fold more consolidated BBWAA electorate would likely produce at least one defection across 30 ballots, and the ~4% chance he loses outright subtracts a bit more. I land slightly below the runs at 0.09.
